issue.title: Athena user supervisord serves unauthenticated multivisor-rpc on 0.0.0.0:8052, and the Multivisor web UI binds 0.0.0.0:8100

task_type_fields.impact: Unauthenticated network control of every bryan-level supervised service on athena, including log reads that may leak secrets. The 8100 web login also travels over plain HTTP on the LAN. This does not escalate to root without the web password, but it is an open control channel on a host breached on 2026-10-17.
task_type_fields.repro:
On athena, 2026-10-23:

```bash
ss -ltn | grep -E ':(8052|8100)\b'          # 0.0.0.0:8052 and 0.0.0.0:8100 LISTEN
grep -n multivisor ~/.config/supervisor/supervisord.conf ~/.config/supervisor/athena.conf
ssh apollo 'timeout 4 bash -c "</dev/tcp/100.87.31.114/8052" && echo open'   # open
```

Bryan's user supervisord (`~/.config/supervisor/supervisord.conf`, `[eventlistener:multivisor-rpc] command=multivisor-rpc --bind *:8052`) serves the multivisor zerorpc bridge on every interface. multivisor-rpc has no authentication, so any LAN or tailnet host can call the user Supervisor API, as can any local account such as `plex`: stop/start/signal programs (rfserver, clipster, the Multivisor web UI), read their logs, or shut down the user supervisord. The Multivisor web UI (`athena.conf`, `multivisor ... --bind *:8100`) is also bound to `0.0.0.0`. It is password-protected but serves plain HTTP on LAN and tailnet, and through the IPC bridge it gives full root-Supervisor control. The only consumer of 8052 found is the local Multivisor web UI (`multivisor.conf` `url=localhost:8052`), so an IPC or `127.0.0.1` bind is likely enough. `multivisor.conf` also points at `hera:8051`/`hera:8052`, a host that is not in the current tailnet inventory.

Fix: move the user bridge to an access-controlled IPC socket (as bob-cli-8u did for root with `ipc:///tmp/supervisor-root-multivisor.sock`) or bind it to `127.0.0.1`, and update `multivisor.conf`. Then decide whether the web UI should be loopback-only behind Tailscale Serve or tailnet-only plus firewall. Verify with the remote probe above. bob-cli-8u covered only the root supervisord bridge (8051); this user-level bridge was out of its scope.

issue.creation_reason: Found by bob-cli-an.land while verifying bob-cli-8u: the root bridge is fixed, but the user-level bridge is reachable from apollo over the tailnet with no authentication.

payload.description: bob-cli-8u moved the root supervisord bridge to an access-controlled IPC socket; this is the same unauthenticated bridge on Bryan's user supervisord, outside 8u's root scope
Both are remaining 0.0.0.0 control listeners on athena found while landing bob-cli-an; firewall work could be coordinated
av kept 8100 tailnet-reachable for this web UI
Lander recheck of task scope before closing for bob-cli-an.6

payload.entry: Verified by bob-cli-an.6 lander 2026-10-23: user multivisor-rpc runs on ipc:///tmp/supervisor-user-multivisor.sock (bryan:bryan srwx------) and no :8052 listener exists. From apollo, 100.87.31.114:8052 is refused and WAN 8052/8100 is filtered; 8100 answers on the tailnet only (decision multivisor_web_access=tailnet; nft table inet athena_multivisor accepts only lo and tailscale0, unit athena-multivisor-boundary active and enabled). Installed .nft/.service/apply script are byte-identical to tailnet c785507. Live supervisord.conf matches user_supervisord.conf.template. verify_user_supervisor.py exits 0 (authenticated Multivisor controls root and user supervisors, /api/data 401 unauthenticated). hera entries kept with no retirement evidence. Separate finding: GET / returns 500 TemplateNotFound in the 2025 pipx install, filed as bob-cli-b4.
